s: All wisdom comes from the Lord. The fear of the Lord is the root of wisdom.
When you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing.
Honour your father and mother. Humility and care for the poor.
Do not turn away the poor. Wisdom tests those who love her.
Do not trust in wealth or delay turning to the Lord.
Be careful in choosing friends. A faithful friend is a strong shelter.
Avoid evil, pride and injustice. Duties to family, priests and the poor.
Prudence in dealing with others.
Advice on women and on choosing companions.
The dangers of pride and the true honour of fearing God.
Do not judge by appearances. All things come from the Lord.
Be careful whom you help and whom you trust.
Choose your companions carefully. The rich and the poor.
The right use of wealth. Blessed is the one who seeks wisdom.
Wisdom comes to those who fear the Lord. God gave humans free choice.
God punishes the wicked and sees everything.
God created humans in his image and gave them understanding and the law.
God's greatness and mercy. Self-control.
Guard your tongue and avoid gossip.
Wise and foolish speech.
Turn away from sin as from a serpent.
Laziness and folly. Keep friendships faithful.
A prayer for help to control the tongue and desires. Warnings about oaths and lust.
Wisdom praises herself: she dwelt in Israel and is found in the law.
Things that please and things that grieve. A good wife and a bad one.
A good wife is a great blessing.
The dangers of dishonest business and of revealing secrets.
Forgive your neighbour's wrong, and your sins will be forgiven when you pray.
Lending, almsgiving and hospitality.
Raising children with discipline. Health is better than wealth.
The use of wealth and good manners at table.
Conduct at banquets. Fear the Lord and keep the law.
The fear of the Lord. Fair treatment of servants.
Dreams are empty; trust in the Lord.
Offerings pleasing to God. The Lord hears the prayer of the humble.
A prayer for God to deliver and gather Israel.
True and false friends, counsellors and self-restraint.
Honour the physician, for the Lord created him. Different trades and their worth.
The scribe who studies the law. A hymn of praise to God's works.
The hardships of human life. Lasting blessings.
Death, and the memory a good name leaves behind.
Things to be ashamed of and not ashamed of. The glory of God in creation.
The sun, moon, stars, snow and sea all show God's glory, and still we cannot praise him enough.
Let us praise famous men: Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Praise of Moses, Aaron and Phinehas.
Praise of Joshua, Caleb, the judges and Samuel.
Praise of Nathan, David and Solomon, and the sins that divided the kingdom.
Praise of Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Isaiah.
Praise of Josiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the twelve prophets, Zerubbabel and Nehemiah.
Praise of Simon the high priest in the glory of the temple worship.
Jesus son of Sirach thanks God for deliverance and tells how he sought wisdom.
